bigIdea: Studio Animae's landing page IS the engine, not a page about it: one warm-black "drawing sheet" where motion is the subject being diagrammed AND something you can physically grab. We graft Concept 3's blueprint discipline (title blocks, dimension lines, self-plotting line work that diagrams real motion-engineering concepts) onto Concept 1's scroll-as-organism spine, then anchor it with Concept 2's hands-on physics so the value prop ("we make software breathe") is proven in your hands rather than claimed. Every section is a different anime.js capability shown as a self-referential demo of the craft: kinetic type, scroll-scrubbed reveals, a self-drawing easing curve, a draggable spring playground that inks its own displacement graph, an orchestrated timeline, exactly one ruled marquee, and a closing title-block CTA. The unifying conceit (the studio diagrams its own motion in front of you, on a single locked dark theme) cannot be lifted onto a generic SaaS template without losing its entire reason to exist.
heroSpec:
Component: Hero. Layout: full-bleed asymmetric title-block stage that fits one viewport. Faint dotted blueprint grid background plus surgical acid registration ticks in the four corners (static SVG, opacity ~0.12). Left two-thirds: oversized font-display headline "We make software breathe." set on a baseline like a drawing title block, max 2 lines. Below it a font-mono kicker "motion-layer engineering / since 2019" (text-faint), one subtext line <=20 words "We engineer the transitions, physics and micro-interactions that make a product feel alive." (text-mist), and ONE primary CTA pill "Start a build" (bg-acid text-ink, rounded-2xl). Right third: a single large SVG of a cubic-bezier ease curve with its control-point handles.

Exact anime.js v4 moment (all inside useAnimeScope, refs not global selectors): on load, text.split(h1Ref, { chars: true, lines: true }); wrap lines in .split-line clip mask; animate(chars, { y: ['110%','0%'], opacity: [0,1], delay: stagger(28, { from: 'center' }), duration: 900, ease: 'outExpo' }). Simultaneously svg.createDrawable on the bezier path + its two handle lines -> animate(draw, { draw: ['0 0','0 1'], duration: 1400, ease: 'inOutQuad' }) so the curve plots itself under/beside the type. Once drawn, const { translateX, translateY } = svg.createMotionPath(curvePath); animate(dotRef, { translateX, translateY, loop: true, duration: 3200, ease: 'inOutSine' }) so a dot rides the exact ease curve forever, dropping faint mono dimension ticks. CTA pill jiggles on pointerenter via animate(pill, { scale: [1, 1.04, 1], ease: createSpring({ stiffness: 140, damping: 9 }) }). The hero literally diagrams what an easing function is. No scroll cue. Mobile: curve diagram moves below the type block, single column, dot loop kept (cheap). Reduced motion (usePrefersReducedMotion gating useAnimeScope enabled flag): chars fully visible at rest, curve drawn at draw '0 1' statically via utils.set, no dot loop, no pill jiggle.

sections.layoutFamily: split editorial (sticky annotated diagram left / scroll-scrubbed spec text right)
sections.animeFeature: onScroll({ sync: 1 }) scrubbing a single timeline of dimension-line + label reveals on a UI element diagram
sections.spec: The page's ONLY eyebrow (covers the next 3 sections): font-mono 'ANATOMY'. Headline h2: 'Every interaction has a spec.' Left column is position:sticky and holds one SVG of a simple UI element (a button/toggle); right column is a scrollable stack of spec lines: trigger, duration, easing, spring, payoff, each a mono label + plain-language value. anime.js: build one createTimeline (paused) that draws each dimension line/callout onto the left SVG (svg.createDrawable per leader line) and fades+rises each right-column spec line; drive it with autoplay: onScroll({ target: sectionRef, enter: 'top top', leave: 'bottom bottom', sync: 1 }) so scrolling scrubs annotations onto the diagram in lockstep. Animate transform/opacity + SVG draw only. Mobile: sticky disabled, diagram stacks above spec lines, timeline still scrubs on scroll. Reduced motion: all dimension lines drawn (utils.set draw '0 1'), all spec lines visible, no onScroll attached.

sections.layoutFamily: bento (exactly 5 cells: 1 wide hero cell + 2 tall + 2 small, asymmetric)
sections.animeFeature: stagger({ grid, from: 'center' }) entrance + per-cell svg.createDrawable line-icon that inks itself on enter, plus createSpring hover micro-bounce
sections.spec: Headline h2: 'What we engineer.' Exactly 5 cells, never 3 equal cards: Transitions (wide hero), Physics (tall), Gesture (tall), State choreography (small), Performance budget (small). Each cell: a hand-plotted phosphor-style line icon as inline SVG, a mono part-number in the corner (e.g. AN-01..AN-05), one line of copy. anime.js: on section enter (standalone onScroll onEnter against sectionRef), run animate(cells, { opacity: [0,1], y: [24,0], scale: [0.96,1], delay: stagger(70, { grid: [3,2], from: 'center' }), ease: 'outExpo' }) and for each cell's icon svg.createDrawable -> animate(draw, { draw: ['0 0','0 1'], duration: 700 }). On pointerenter per cell, animate(icon, { scale: [1,1.08,1], ease: createSpring({ stiffness: 130, damping: 10 }) }). Mobile: bento collapses to a single column stack, icons still ink on enter. Reduced motion: cells visible, icons drawn statically, no hover bounce.

sections.layoutFamily: draggable-playground (single bordered bounds canvas, signature interactive)
sections.animeFeature: createDraggable + createSpring releaseEase, dragged node trails a live svg.createDrawable displacement graph, neighbor-nudge animate() spring radiating from grab
sections.spec: THE signature section and the required draggable+spring playground. Headline h2: 'Drag the mass. Read the curve.' One large bordered tray (rounded-3xl, border border-ink-3) containing one prominent acid mass node plus ~10 secondary tokens. createDraggable(massRef, { container: boundsRef, releaseEase: createSpring({ stiffness: 120, damping: 12 }) }); onGrab nudges neighbors via animate(neighbors, { x: stagger(['-0.6rem','0.6rem']), ease: createSpring({ stiffness: 90, damping: 8 }) }) radiating from grab point; while dragging/onRelease, ink the mass trajectory as a live SVG path using svg.createDrawable so a displacement-over-time graph draws itself, with mono readouts for stiffness/damping updating in the corner. A 'tip the tray' button runs a createTimer-driven gravity sweep sending all tokens sliding and settling with staggered spring damping. Pure feedback-motivated motion. Mobile: tray full-width, touch drag enabled, neighbor count reduced; trajectory graph kept. Reduced motion: drag DISABLED, tokens static in a tidy resting layout, a pre-drawn example curve shown statically, no timer sweep.

sections.layoutFamily: timeline (vertical numbered rail with a self-drawing spine)
sections.animeFeature: createTimeline orchestrated sequence with labels + relative offsets, plus a createDrawable spine that draws as each phase lands and a spring-eased progress dot
sections.spec: The required createTimeline orchestrated section. Headline h2: 'How a build gets drawn.' Four phases on a vertical rail: Brief, Spec, Prototype, Ship, each with a mono duration callout and one line of copy. anime.js: one createTimeline({ defaults: { ease: 'outExpo', duration: 700 } }) with labels per phase: draw the connecting spine via svg.createDrawable (animate draw '0 0'->'0 1' across the timeline), stagger each phase marker + card in on its own beat using relative positions ('+=150', '<'), and send a progress dot down the spine with ease: createSpring({ stiffness: 100, damping: 14 }). Trigger the timeline play via onScroll onEnter against sectionRef (play once). Mobile: rail stays vertical (already single column), cards full-width. Reduced motion: spine drawn statically, all phases visible, dot parked at end, timeline never plays.

sections.layoutFamily: marquee (the single allowed continuous kinetic band, baseline-ruled)
sections.animeFeature: continuous animate() translateX loop with seamless wrap, velocity reacting to scroll direction via onScroll onUpdate
sections.spec: The ONE and only marquee on the entire page. A single ruled measurement baseline with font-display verbs and acid tick separators: 'EASING / SPRING / GESTURE / CHOREOGRAPHY / 60FPS /' (real hyphens/slashes only, zero em or en dashes). anime.js: duplicate the band content for seamless wrap; animate(bandRef, { x: ['0%','-50%'], loop: true, ease: 'linear', duration: 18000 }); attach a standalone onScroll({ onUpdate: (self) => modulate playbackRate / direction from scroll velocity }) so scrolling down speeds it forward, up nudges it backward. Exactly one band, no second marquee anywhere. Mobile: same single band, slightly larger duration for legibility. Reduced motion: band rendered static (no loop), content not duplicated for animation, fully readable.

sections.animeFeature: text.split line reveal + createTimeline closing sequence with a createDrawable signature underline stroke and the hero breath/curve exhaling flat
sections.spec: The required final CTA. Headline h2: 'Let us draw your motion layer.' (real words, no dash). ONE CTA pill 'Start a build' (bg-acid text-ink, identical label to nav + hero per brief). Mono footer arranged as a drawing title block: studio name, sheet no., revision, date. anime.js: a small recap SVG curve sits behind; on section enter run one createTimeline that (1) text.split the headline into lines and animate y:['110%','0%'] opacity:[0,1] with stagger, (2) draws a single acid underline 'signature' stroke via svg.createDrawable as the final beat, (3) lets the recap curve morphTo a flat baseline then settle (svg.morphTo) as an exhale, closing the breath metaphor. CTA pill keeps the spring jiggle on pointerenter. Trigger once via onScroll onEnter. Mobile: centered single column, title-block fields stack. Reduced motion: headline visible, underline drawn statically, curve flat at rest, no jiggle.
